title: Cicoria Saltata
subtitle: sauteed bitter greens with garlic, chilli and olive oil
excerpt: Cicoria saltata is a southern Italian side dish of bitter greens quickly sautéed with sliced garlic, dried chilli and a generous amount of olive oil, then finished with a squeeze of lemon. The whole dish takes ten minutes and works alongside almost any meat or fish. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Cicoria saltata, or sautéed chicory, is one of the most common vegetable preparations in Lazio and throughout the Italian south. Wild cicoria was foraged from fields and roadsides and brought home to be blanched and then fried in olive oil with garlic and chilli. The method applies to most bitter greens and is one of the foundational side dishes of cucina povera.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian for chicory or wild bitter greens, used in southern Italian cooking as a side vegetable or in paired dishes like fave e cicoria.
Italian for garlic and oil, the classic simple flavouring base used across Italian vegetable and pasta dishes.

content.text: saltata is as simple as Italian cooking gets: blanched bitter greens tossed in a pan with

and a pinch of dried chilli. The blanching step is not optional, it softens the greens and takes the sharpest edge off the bitterness before the sauté concentrates the flavour. Serves 4 as a side dish.
Radicchio works well here as a substitute for wild cicoria. It holds its shape in the pan and has the right level of bitterness. A squeeze of lemon at the end lifts the whole dish.
Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Add the radicchio and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until wilted and tender. Drain well and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until the garlic is softened but not coloured.
Add the drained greens to the pan. Toss to coat in the oil. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and the edges are just beginning to crisp.
Season to taste. Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve immediately.

attrs.symptom: Greens are soggy and steaming in the pan
attrs.cause: Too much water was left in the greens after blanching
attrs.fix: Squeeze the blanched greens very firmly in your hands or press them in a colander before adding to the hot oil

attrs.symptom: Garlic is brown and bitter before the greens go in
attrs.cause: The heat was too high or the garlic was left too long
attrs.fix: Keep the heat at medium and watch the garlic closely. It needs only 1 minute to soften. Add the greens as soon as it turns pale golden

attrs.symptom: Dish tastes bland despite garlic and chilli
attrs.cause: The greens were not seasoned and the lemon was skipped
attrs.fix: Season well after cooking and do not skip the lemon. It sharpens everything and makes the flavours stand out

content.text: Cicoria saltata is a daily side dish across Lazio, Campania and Puglia. In Rome it is served alongside fried foods at traditional trattorias. In Puglia it is the partner to the broad bean purée in fave e cicoria. It takes almost no effort and can be on the table in ten minutes. Any bitter green works: radicchio, cavolo nero, or whatever looks good at the market.
